results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004952 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. The calyx is the part closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes, and the mushroom body lobe system consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages. VFB holds extensive data related to the mushroom body, including information on neurons with some part in the mushroom body, neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body, parts of the mushroom body, and images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body, with over 22,000 images available.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response:
In the adult Drosophila brain, several types of Kenyon cells exist. According to VFB, these include alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes. The gamma Kenyon cells, for example, are known to innervate only the gamma lobe in the adult. VFB holds a range of data related to gamma Kenyon cells, including images, subclasses, expression patterns, scRNAseq data, and transgene expression data. Specifically, there are [3](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100247,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of gamma Kenyon cell") available images of gamma Kenyon cells, [10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100247,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of gamma Kenyon cell") subclasses, [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100247,ExpressionOverlapsHere "Run in VFB: Expression patterns overlapping gamma Kenyon cell") expression patterns overlapping with gamma Kenyon cells, [6](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100247,anatScRNAseqQuery "Run in VFB: scRNAseq data for gamma Kenyon cell") scRNAseq datasets, and 23 transgene expression datasets.

results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response:
The main components of the Drosophila central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the three paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. 
The central complex is associated with a range of functions, including spatial memory and navigation, as well as the control of locomotor behaviors. However, specific functions associated with each component are not detailed in the provided evidence.
VFB holds a range of data related to the central complex, including images of the [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004913 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain"), information on neurons with processes in the central complex, and details of transgene expression in this brain region. results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The [LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") visual neuron type is a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron. It has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. This arrangement allows it to detect looming (expansion) stimuli and its activity elicits a jump escape response. LPLC2 connects to various neurons, including adult cholinergic neurons, T5c neurons, and transmedullary neurons. 
Available VFB data includes information on over 14,000 neurons, including LPLC2, which has the ID [1813403998](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open 1813403998 in Virtual Fly Brain") (VFB_jrch0fva).

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior (Thomas and Wyman, 1984). It has a distinct anatomy, with a large descending axon that arborizes in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center. There is one giant fiber neuron per hemisphere, with its large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum (Koto et al., 1981). The giant fiber neuron can be identified by its large descending axon, which is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective (Koto et al., 1981; Power, 1948).

In terms of connectivity, VFB holds extensive data on the downstream and upstream connectivity classes for the giant fiber neuron ([DNp01](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open DNp01 in Virtual Fly Brain")), with [361](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") downstream and [435](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") upstream connectivity classes available. Additionally, VFB has [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") available images of DNp01 and data on transgene expression in DNp01 from [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") different sources.

Several driver lines are available for the giant fiber neuron, including P{VT046265-GAL4}, which has a characterized expression pattern. Relevant publications on the giant fiber neuron include those by Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), and Sturner et al. (2025), which provide further information on its anatomy, connectivity, and role in jump escape behavior.

Overall, the giant fiber neuron is a well-characterized neuron with a unique anatomy and connectivity profile, and VFB provides extensive data and resources for its study.
